problem.statement: devkit's ship gate runs several LLM reviewers over the WHOLE staged diff on every attempt. After a FAIL the agent fixes one thing and re-ships; the diff hash changes so reviewers re-run on the entire diff and, being stochastic, often surface a NEW finding in code they previously passed. Result: 23 branches needed >=20 attempts (max 55), top branch cost $466 in judge calls, ~15 min per attempt. Proposed fix: (1) incremental review of only code amended since the last attempt; (2) on the first attempt, chunk the diff into ~300-LOC slices reviewed in parallel, possibly on a cheaper model.
problem.restatedFrame: Ship-gate retries are expensive because each retry re-sends a reviewer's entire domain diff and re-pays a stochastic LLM judgment on bytes that already passed, so the fix is architected as a windowing problem: show less code per attempt (delta-only on retries, LOC-chunked fan-out on the first pass).
assumedConstraints: Reviewer granularity (one verdict per reviewer over its whole domain diff) is fixed; the only lever considered is how much of that diff is shown per attempt.

The churn is attributed mainly to reviewer stochasticity re-flagging previously-passed, unchanged code, rather than to reviewer imprecision on genuinely new fix code or to non-LLM (deterministic) gate blocks.
The cited numbers (23 branches, max 55 attempts, $466 top branch, ~15 min/attempt) are treated as accurate inputs rather than something to re-derive from telemetry before scoping a fix.
Shrinking the first-attempt reviewer's context to ~300-LOC chunks on a cheaper model is assumed roughly recall-neutral; the cross-chunk blind spot is named as a risk but not measured.

frameChallenge.upstreamChoice: The 2026-07-02 review-gate-in-chain ruling to cache a reviewer PASS as one SHA256 over its WHOLE per-reviewer diff (never per-file/per-hunk) — refined since (diffCacheIdentity's sentry-only normalization, sc-1437's identity salts) but never repartitioned to a finer grain — even though judge-verdict-cache-scope (2026-08-07) already proved that re-keying at a NARROWER altitude (branch+message for completeness) eliminates the identical repeat-cost problem, and gate-verdict-attribution already computes per-file diff_sha256 for telemetry that a finer cache partition would need.

questions.finding: No declared reference checkout, but peer LLM-diff-reviewer tools are real and reachable: CodeRabbit's auto_incremental_review re-reviews only commits since the last review (confirmed via docs + 20+ production adopters found on GitHub); PR-Agent/Qodo (open source, cloneable) compresses/chunks large diffs. These are genuine peer consumers of the same problem class.

No — `claude -p` is a stateless one-shot completion call with no session/diff memory; the underlying dependency exposes no native 'diff since last invocation' mode. Any windowing has to live in devkit's own retry logic, so this isn't a case of picking the harder of two dependency-native paths.

Must every retry re-send the reviewer's WHOLE domain diff? No. Devkit's own architecture already treats cache granularity as adjustable ('cached at the altitude of the question', judge-verdict-cache-scope) — the whole-diff-per-reviewer boundary is a chosen cache partition, not an inherent property of LLM review.

Confirmed absent by direct code read: run-review.mts computes `diffs = selected.map((s) => gitCached(cwd, [], s.files))` — one full diff per reviewer's entire file set — and no file in gate-engine/review/**, reviewers.mts, ship-branch.sh, or reship.sh carries an attempt-index or since-last-attempt delta computation. Lens-split (the closest analog) divides by CONCERN over the SAME full diff, not by code region.

CodeRabbit (incremental review), PR-Agent (diff compression/chunking for large PRs), Cursor BugBot (8-way parallel pass + majority vote for precision), and an academic Multi-Review ensemble paper (2025) all solve adjacent slices of this same class of problem in production or peer-reviewed work.

Real but partially unverified cost: this machine's telemetry sink (67,950 events) shows 19 branches with >=20 ship_attempt rows and a max of 49 on one branch — same order of magnitude as the cited 23/55 but not an exact match (consistent with the known per-machine-sink caveat). New failure surface: showing a reviewer only a new hunk (not the full file) is a STRICTLY WEAKER guarantee than devkit's current cache, which only skips a reviewer when its ENTIRE domain diff is byte-identical — incremental windowing would introduce a new class of contract-blindness the current architecture does not yet tolerate. Repeat-patch alarm: >=2 prior rounds already patched this exact 'retries repay reviewers for unchanged work' axis (prefix-cache, message-scope cache, sc-1437 identity salts, diffCacheIdentity normalization, correctness-lens-split's two-round A/B) — the frame, not the next patch, is the recurring signal.

Yes — the whole-per-reviewer-diff cache-key granularity chosen in review-gate-in-chain (2026-07-02) is the upstream decision. Revisiting it toward per-file (or per-hunk) partitioning — reusing lens-split's existing merge/aggregate machinery and the per-file diff_sha256 gate-verdict-attribution already emits — captures most of proposal (1)'s cost win without inventing new windowing machinery or its contract-blindness risk.

evidence.claim: A reviewer PASS is cached as one hash over the reviewer's WHOLE domain diff; only a byte-identical diff skips review — by explicit design.
evidence.quote: Cache key for a PASS verdict: reviewer identity + devkit version + the exact bytes of its staged domain diff... That skip is BY DESIGN

evidence.claim: Each reviewer's diff is computed once over ALL its domain files, not per-file or per-hunk — confirms no incremental/since-last-attempt windowing exists anywhere in the ship/review path.

Devkit's own correctness reviewer already false-blocks ~14% of clean diffs, model-invariantly, with the fix (K-sample self-consistency) ruled but explicitly unbuilt/paused — a second, independent driver of repeated FAILs that incremental review does not touch.
evidence.quote: the single-pass correctness reviewer false-blocks ~14% of clean diffs... precision cannot be bought by a bigger model (model-invariant: haiku 0.86 = sonnet 0.86).

evidence.claim: Devkit already solved an identical repeat-cost problem for the completeness judge by re-keying its cache at a narrower altitude (branch+message) instead of exact bytes — proving cache-granularity repartitioning is a proven, already-shipped in-repo lever.
evidence.quote: A confident PASS is cached at the altitude of the question the judge answers, not uniformly on the evidence bytes.

evidence.claim: Per-file diff hashes are already computed and emitted for telemetry attribution — the primitive a per-file cache partition would need already exists, just not wired into the verdict-cache key.
evidence.quote: Every SELECTED reviewer emits review_scope BEFORE the judge runs — files, diff_sha256, file count and hash, and cached

suggestedNextStep.detail: Split into three separable stories instead of one windowing project. (1) Repartition the existing per-reviewer review-cache to per-file granularity, reusing lens-split's merge/aggregate machinery and the per-file diff_sha256 gate-verdict-attribution already computes — this captures proposal (1)'s cost win (an unrelated file's change no longer forces full re-review) without incremental-windowing's new contract-blindness risk, since each touched file's FULL diff is still shown, just untouched files are skipped. (2) Scope first-attempt LOC-chunking for very large diffs (proposal 2) as its own investigation — real prior art exists (PR-Agent's chunking, Cursor BugBot's parallel-pass ensembles) but it solves first-attempt latency on huge PRs, a different problem from retry churn, and needs its own risk analysis for cross-chunk blindness. (3) Before committing engineering budget, verify the cited numbers against the full gate-events.jsonl telemetry (this sink alone shows 19 branches / max 49, not 23/55) and measure what fraction of repeat FAILs land on files/hunks that did NOT change between attempts (the churn this proposal targets) versus genuinely new findings on the fix itself or on deterministic (non-LLM) gates — correctness-reviewer-precision's already-documented ~14% model-invariant false-block rate may be the larger, unaddressed driver.

summary: The stated mechanism (whole-diff re-review forces stochastic re-flagging on retries) is real and code-confirmed — reviewers.mts/run-review.mts cache and re-diff at the granularity of one reviewer's ENTIRE domain, never per-file or per-hunk, so any unrelated fix invalidates the whole verdict. But devkit already has a proven, cheaper, safer answer to this exact shape of problem: judge-verdict-cache-scope re-keyed the completeness judge's cache to a narrower altitude (branch+message) instead of exact bytes, and gate-verdict-attribution already computes per-file diff hashes for telemetry. Repartitioning the domain-reviewer cache to per-file granularity would capture most of proposal (1)'s savings while avoiding a new correctness risk that true incremental windowing introduces (showing only a new hunk, not the surrounding file, is a strictly weaker guarantee than today's full-diff-identity cache). Proposal (2)'s LOC-chunking targets a different problem (first-attempt latency on huge PRs, not retry churn) and has real external prior art (PR-Agent, Cursor BugBot) but needs its own scoping. Separately, devkit's own correctness-reviewer-precision decision already documents a ~14% model-invariant false-block rate with its fix (K-sample self-consistency) ruled but unbuilt — likely a larger, independent driver of the attempt counts than diff-window size. The cited numbers are directionally corroborated by local telemetry (19 branches/max 49 vs cited 23/55) but not exactly verified. Recommend reframing into the cache-repartition story (cheap, low-risk, reuses existing machinery), a separate chunking story for huge first attempts, and re-deriving the actual telemetry before scoping either.
